category: RF & Wave Optics I: Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain feature nodes and RF/optics part and material libraries
description: Domain, boundary, edge, point and pair nodes of the Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain interface (emw in the RF Module, ewfd in the Wave Optics Module) - material models, periodic structures, far-field domains, thin-layer conditions and sources - plus the module-specific Part and Material Libraries. Java type strings and property names were taken from the COMSOL 6.4 plugin definitions and Application Library models.

tools.name: Interface Settings (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: The Settings window of the Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain node decides how the time-harmonic curl-curl equation for E is set up: Formulation (Full field or Scattered field with a background wave), the field components solved for in 2D/2D axisymmetry, the out-of-plane wave number or azimuthal mode number, the solver Methodology (Robust, Intermediate or Fast - the default), port sweeps, the port formulation and the discretization order. It also controls the physics-controlled mesh (maximum element size from the study frequency) and offers toolbar buttons that add lossy boundary features from the materials or cut the 3D model in half with a PEC/PMC symmetry plane.
tools.usage: Model Builder > Component 1 > Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain (emw) > Settings. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").prop("components").set("components", "outofplane"); physics("emw").prop("BackgroundField").set("SolveFor", "scatteredField"); physics("emw").prop("MeshControl").set("SizeControlParameter", "UserDefined"); physics("emw").prop("Toolbar").runCommand("lossyFeaturesFromMaterials")

parameters.name: Formulation (BackgroundField/SolveFor)
parameters.description: fullField (default) or scatteredField; with scattered field choose the Background wave type (WaveType: userdef, GaussianBeam, LinearPol, and circularly/linearly polarized plane waves in 2D axisymmetry).

parameters.name: Electric field components solved for (components)
parameters.description: 2D/2D-axi only: threecomponent (default), outofplane (TE-type, E normal to the plane) or inplane (TM-type).

parameters.name: Out-of-plane wave number / Azimuthal mode number (outofplanewavenumber/mFloquet)
parameters.description: kz for 2D, integer m for 2D axisymmetry; not used in Mode Analysis where it is the eigenvalue.

parameters.name: Methodology
parameters.description: Robust, Intermediate or Fast (default) - selects the generated solver configuration.

parameters.name: Port Sweep Settings (PortSweepSettings)
parameters.description: useSweep, sweep parameter name (PortParamName, default PortName), ExportTouchstone and file; Configure Sweep Settings adds the parametric sweep.

parameters.name: Port formulation (advanced)
parameters.description: Weak formulation (default, adds one scalar DOF per S-parameter) or Constraint-based.

parameters.name: Physics-controlled mesh (MeshControl)
parameters.description: SizeControlParameter FromStudy | UserDefined | Frequency | Wavelength; ResolveWaveInLossyMedia; RefineConductiveEdges; AddFarFieldBoundaryLayers.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Electric field shape order Linear ... Septic, each also as 'type 2'; default Quadratic.

tools.notes: With 'From study' the maximum element size in free space is lambda0/5 in 3D and lambda0/8 in 2D at the highest study frequency (quadratic elements; half for linear, 2.25x for cubic), divided by sqrt(epsr*mur) in dielectrics; 'Resolve wave in lossy media' meshes lossy boundaries with min(skin depth/2, lambda0/5). In 2D axisymmetry a covariant formulation is used, so evaluate emw.Ephi rather than the dependent variable. The Wave Optics Module uses the same interface under the tag ewfd and adds the Wavelength Domain study.

tools.name: Refractive Index Model (Wave Equation, Electric, Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Electric displacement field model of the Wave Equation, Electric node in which the material is described by the real refractive index n and the imaginary part k, giving epsr = (n - i*k)^2 with mur = 1 and sigma = 0. It is the natural choice for optical materials from the Optical Material Library and for anisotropic crystals, where a Diagonal/Full tensor together with a rotated coordinate system orients the index ellipsoid. Under COMSOL's time-harmonic sign convention a lossy material must have positive k.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain > Wave Equation, Electric > Electric Displacement Field > Electric displacement field model: Refractive index. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").feature("wee1").set("DisplacementFieldModel", "RefractiveIndex"); set("n_mat", "userdef"); set("n", ...); set("ki_mat", "userdef"); set("ki", ...)

parameters.name: Refractive index n (n, n_mat)
parameters.description: From material (default) or User defined: Isotropic, Diagonal, Symmetric or Full.

parameters.name: Refractive index, imaginary part k (ki, ki_mat)
parameters.description: Absorption; positive for loss.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: Orients the principal axes of a diagonal index tensor (index ellipsoid).

tools.notes: Relative permittivity, Refractive index, Loss tangent (angle or dissipation factor) and Dielectric loss models can be synchronized - material data given in one form is converted automatically to the model selected in the feature. The same model list is available in Impedance, Transition and Layered boundary conditions (isotropic only there). For transient interfaces only the real part of n is used.

tools.name: Loss Tangent and Dielectric Loss Models (Wave Equation, Electric, Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Three lossy-dielectric forms of the electric displacement field model: Loss tangent, loss angle (real permittivity eps' and loss angle delta), Loss tangent, dissipation factor (eps' and tan(delta)) and Dielectric loss (eps' and eps'', with epsr = eps' - j*eps''). They assume zero conductivity and are the usual way to enter PCB substrate and ceramic data sheets, e.g. the Rogers and Isola laminates in the RF Material Library. Positive eps'' or tan(delta) means loss under the COMSOL sign convention.
tools.usage: Wave Equation, Electric > Electric displacement field model: Loss tangent, loss angle | Loss tangent, dissipation factor | Dielectric loss. API: feature("wee1").set("DisplacementFieldModel", "LossTangentDF"); set("epsilonPrimDF_mat", "userdef"); set("epsilonPrimDF", ...); set("tanDelta_mat", "userdef"); set("tanDelta", "0.0002")

parameters.name: epsilonPrimLA / delta
parameters.description: Real permittivity and loss angle for 'Loss tangent, loss angle' (DisplacementFieldModel LossTangent).

parameters.name: epsilonPrimDF / tanDelta
parameters.description: Real permittivity and dissipation factor for 'Loss tangent, dissipation factor' (LossTangentDF).

parameters.name: epsilonPrim / epsilonBis
parameters.description: eps' and eps'' for 'Dielectric loss'.

tools.notes: Frequency-dependent data can be entered as a function of the variable freq when that argument is marked as a Frequency model input in the material property group. For conductor losses use sigma in the Conduction Current section or an Impedance/Transition boundary condition instead.

tools.name: Drude-Lorentz Dispersion Model (Wave Equation, Electric, Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Frequency-domain dispersion model epsr(omega) = eps_inf + sum_j f_j*omega_P^2/(omega_0j^2 - omega^2 + i*Gamma_j*omega), used for metals (plasmonics), doped semiconductors and resonant metamaterial inclusions whose permittivity varies strongly over the sweep. It is entered directly in Wave Equation, Electric so a Frequency Domain or Wavelength Domain sweep evaluates the correct complex permittivity at each point without an interpolation table.
tools.usage: Wave Equation, Electric > Electric displacement field model: Drude-Lorentz dispersion model. API: feature("wee1").set("DisplacementFieldModel", "DrudeLorentzDispersionModel"); set("epsilonInf", ...); set("omegap", "omega_p")

parameters.name: Relative permittivity, high frequency eps_inf (epsilonInf)
parameters.description: User defined (default) or From material; tensor allowed.

parameters.name: Plasma frequency omega_P (omegap)
parameters.description: rad/s; default 0.

parameters.name: Oscillator table
parameters.description: Rows of Oscillator strength f_j, Resonance frequency omega_0j and Damping in time Gamma_j (rad/s); a row with omega_0j = 0 gives a Drude (free-electron) term.

tools.notes: In the transient interfaces (temw/ewt) the same physics is modelled with Drude-Lorentz Polarization subnodes that solve an auxiliary ODE for each oscillator. Check the sign convention of published data (exp(-i*omega*t) versus COMSOL's exp(+j*omega*t)).

tools.name: Debye and Wideband Debye Dispersion Models (Wave Equation, Electric, Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Relaxation-type dispersion models for polar dielectrics: the Debye model epsr = eps_inf + sum_k Delta_eps_k/(1 + i*omega*tau_k) with a table of permittivity contributions and relaxation times, and the Wideband Debye (Djordjevic-Sarkar) model that spreads a total variation Delta_eps logarithmically between two angular frequencies omega_1 and omega_2. The wideband model is the standard causal description of FR-4 and similar PCB laminates over many decades of frequency.
tools.usage: Wave Equation, Electric > Electric displacement field model: Debye dispersion model | Wideband Debye model (also available in Impedance/Transition boundary conditions for Debye).

parameters.name: Relative permittivity, high frequency eps_inf
parameters.description: User defined (default) or From material.

parameters.name: Debye table
parameters.description: Relative permittivity contribution Delta_eps_k and Relaxation time tau_k (s) per row.

parameters.name: Relative permittivity contribution Delta_eps (deltaEpsilon)
parameters.description: Wideband Debye: total variation of the real permittivity.

parameters.name: Lower / Upper angular frequency limit (omega1, omega2)
parameters.description: Wideband Debye limits; defaults 1e5 rad/s and 1e12 rad/s.

tools.example:
Wideband FR-4 substrate for a microstrip S-parameter sweep 0.1-20 GHz:
1. Wave Equation, Electric 2 (substrate domains) > Electric displacement field model = Wideband Debye model.
2. eps_inf = 3.9, Delta_eps = 0.6, omega1 = 1e5[rad/s], omega2 = 1e12[rad/s].
3. Run a Frequency Domain or Adaptive Frequency Sweep study and plot emw.S21dB.
tools.notes: Both models are causal (Kramers-Kronig consistent), which matters when the frequency result is later transformed to the time domain or exported to a circuit simulator via Touchstone.

tools.name: Magnetic Losses and Conduction Current Options (Wave Equation, Electric, Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: The Magnetic Field and Conduction Current sections of Wave Equation, Electric complete the material description: the constitutive relation Relative permeability (tensor, From material or Effective medium) or Magnetic losses (mur = mu' - j*mu''), and the electric conductivity given directly, as a Linearized resistivity rho = rho0*(1 + alpha*(T - Tref)), from an Effective Medium mixture or from Archie's law. Ferrites (with a full permeability tensor), absorbers and lossy tissue are modelled here.
tools.usage: Wave Equation, Electric > Magnetic Field: Constitutive relation; Conduction Current: Electric conductivity. API: feature("wee1").set("ConstitutiveRelationH", "RelativePermeability"); set("mur_mat", "userdef"); set("mur", ...); set("sigma_mat", "userdef"); set("sigma", ...)

parameters.name: Relative permeability mur (mur, mur_mat)
parameters.description: Isotropic, Diagonal, Symmetric or Full; gyrotropic ferrite tensors go in the Full matrix.

parameters.name: Magnetic losses mu', mu'' (murPrim, murBis)
parameters.description: Complex permeability; positive mu'' for loss.

parameters.name: Electric conductivity sigma (sigma, sigma_mat)
parameters.description: From material, User defined, Linearized resistivity (rho0, alpha, Tref), Effective medium or Archie's law.

tools.example:
Magnetized ferrite in a circulator: Wave Equation, Electric 2 > Relative permeability = User defined, Full, with mur = {mur_xx,-mur_xy,0, mur_xy,mur_xx,0, 0,0,1} from Polder-tensor parameters.
Application Libraries: RF_Module/Ferrimagnetic_Devices/lossy_circulator_3d, RF_Module/Ferrimagnetic_Devices/circulator
tools.notes: The Magnetic Field section is only shown for the Relative permittivity / loss models, not when Refractive index is chosen (which assumes mur = 1, sigma = 0). Linearized resistivity makes sigma temperature dependent, which couples naturally with Microwave Heating.

tools.name: Divergence Constraint (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Subnode of Wave Equation, Electric that adds a divergence condition on the electric field (a gauge-like stabilization) for low frequencies, where the displacement/total current term in the wave equation becomes numerically insignificant and the curl-curl operator alone is singular. Use it when a Frequency Domain emw model must also be run far below the first resonance (quasi-static limit), or in Electromagnetic Waves, Transient models with very slow excitations.
tools.usage: Right-click Wave Equation, Electric > Divergence Constraint. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").feature("wee1").create("dic1", "DivergenceConstraint", 3)

parameters.name: Divergence condition variable scaling psi0
parameters.description: Default 1 kg/(m*s^3*A) in emw and Microwave Heating; 1 A/m in Electromagnetic Waves, Transient.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("emw").feature("wee1").create("dic1", "DivergenceConstraint", 3);
// broadband sweep of an RF coil from 1 kHz to 300 MHz: the constraint keeps the low-frequency end well conditioned
tools.notes: Adds an extra scalar Lagrange-multiplier field, increasing DOFs. For genuinely quasi-static problems the AC/DC Module Magnetic Fields interface is usually cheaper.

tools.name: Effective Medium (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Subnode (PorousMedia type) that builds the conductivity, relative permittivity and/or relative permeability of a domain from a mixture of up to five materials with given volume fractions. Each property can use a volume average, a volume average of the inverse (for example resistivity) or a power-law mixing rule. Use it for composites, moist or porous materials and loaded absorbers when only the constituent properties are known.
tools.usage: Wave Equation, Electric > set Relative permittivity / Relative permeability / Electric conductivity to 'Effective medium' > right-click > Effective Medium. API: feature("wee1").create("pm1", "PorousMedia", 3)

parameters.name: Number of materials
parameters.description: 1-5; each is Domain material or any material node, with volume fraction theta_i (should sum to 1).

parameters.name: Effective Electric Conductivity / Relative Permittivity / Relative Permeability
parameters.description: Volume average, Volume average of inverse, or Power law; values From material or User defined.

tools.example:
Moist wood slab in a microwave dryer:
1. Wave Equation, Electric 2 > Relative permittivity = Effective medium.
2. Effective Medium 1: Number of materials 2 - Material 1 = Wood (theta1 = 0.7), Material 2 = Water (theta2 = 0.3), permittivity by Power law.
tools.notes: Also available in Electromagnetic Waves, Transient. For a conductivity described by fluid saturation and porosity use the Archie's Law subnode instead.

tools.name: Archie's Law (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Conductivity subnode that computes the effective electric conductivity of a nonconductive porous medium saturated (fully or partly) by a conductive liquid from Archie's law, sigma = sigma_L * S_L^n * eps_p^m. It is used in geophysical electromagnetics such as marine controlled-source EM surveys and ground-penetrating radar, where rock porosity and brine saturation control the losses.
tools.usage: Wave Equation, Electric > Conduction Current: Electric conductivity = Archie's law > right-click > Archie's Law. API: feature("wee1").create("arl1", "ArchiesLaw", 3)

parameters.name: Electric conductivity sigma_L
parameters.description: Fluid conductivity, From material or User defined (can be temperature dependent).

parameters.name: Cementation exponent m
parameters.description: Dimensionless rock parameter.

parameters.name: Saturation exponent n
parameters.description: Dimensionless.

parameters.name: Fluid saturation S_L / Porosity eps_p
parameters.description: Volume fraction of pores and the fraction filled with fluid.

tools.example:
Seabed sediment layer in a CSEM model: Conduction Current = Archie's law, sigma_L = 3.2[S/m] (seawater), m = 2, n = 2, S_L = 1, eps_p = 0.4.
Related Application Library model: RF_Module/Scattering_and_RCS/marine_csem
tools.notes: Available in the Frequency Domain and Transient electromagnetic-wave interfaces; see 'Archie's Law Theory' in the RF Module User's Guide.

tools.name: External Current Density (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Domain source that adds an externally generated current density Je to Ohm's law, J = sigma*E + j*omega*D + Je, and therefore to the wave equation. Use it for volumetric sources whose current distribution is known in advance - a prescribed antenna current, an impressed current from another physics, or a distributed excitation in 2D - instead of a port.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > External Current Density. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("ecd1", "ExternalCurrentDensity", 3)

parameters.name: External current density Je
parameters.description: Vector components in A/m^2 (x, y, z in 3D).

tools.notes: No S-parameters are defined for this source. For point-like or line sources use Electric Point Dipole, Edge Current or Line Current (Out-of-Plane); for surface currents use Surface Current Density.

tools.name: Far-Field Domain, Inhomogeneous (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: 3D far-field domain for radiators or scatterers sitting on a substrate: it has default Superstrate and Substrate subnodes (each a homogeneous, isotropic domain group) and a Far-Field Calculation subnode, and computes the far field in the presence of the planar interface instead of assuming a homogeneous surrounding medium. The interface between superstrate and substrate must be flat and normal to a Cartesian axis. It generates normEfar, normdBEfar, Efar components, axialRatioInhg and maximum directivity maxDInhg variables.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Far-Field Domain, Inhomogeneous (3D only), then set the Substrate subnode selection. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("ffi1", "FarFieldDomainInhomogeneous", 3)

parameters.name: Superstrate (sup1)
parameters.description: Default subnode; all domains, cannot be edited; the upper half-space medium.

parameters.name: Substrate (sub1)
parameters.description: Default subnode with empty selection; select the substrate domain group; defines the interface normal.

parameters.name: Far-Field Calculation (ffc1)
parameters.description: Boundaries enclosing the structure (adjacent to the PML), Far-field variable name (default Efar).

tools.notes: At most one Symmetry Plane may be used with this feature. Default Radiation Pattern plots in a Polar Plot Group are generated automatically. For a homogeneous surrounding use the ordinary Far-Field Domain.

tools.name: Periodic Structure (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Domain node that sets up a complete periodic unit-cell simulation in one step: it automatically adds two Periodic Port subnodes on the excitation and listener faces, a Floquet Periodic Condition for every remaining pair of parallel boundaries and a Reference Direction subnode, while all angle, polarization and power inputs are entered once on the parent. An 'Add Diffraction Orders' button creates the Diffraction Order ports for all propagating orders. Use it for gratings, metasurfaces, frequency selective surfaces, absorbers and photonic-crystal slabs, including hexagonal unit cells.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Periodic Structure (3D and 2D). API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("ps1", "PeriodicStructure", 3); physics("emw").feature("ps1").runCommand("addDiffractionOrders")

parameters.name: Excited Port Selection
parameters.description: Boundary that is (part of) the excited port; its normal defines the structure axis a0, which should be aligned with a Cartesian axis.

parameters.name: Port Handling (addListenerPort, DiffractionOrderSpecification, n1, n2)
parameters.description: Add listener port; diffraction orders From current parameters or All angles (default); refractive index at excited/listener port From adjacent domain or User defined.

parameters.name: Polarization (Polarization, LinearPol, CircularPol, etaTM)
parameters.description: LinearPol with TE/TM/Mixed (TM power fraction), CircularPol rhcp/lhcp, or UserDefined E/H amplitude.

parameters.name: Angles of incidence (alpha1_inc, alpha2_inc / alpha_inc)
parameters.description: 3D elevation and azimuth; 2D single angle of incidence.

parameters.name: Port input power Pin
parameters.description: Power of the incident plane wave per unit cell.

tools.notes: Periodic Port and Floquet Periodic Condition subnodes need no settings of their own. Reflectance/transmittance per order are available as emw.Rorder_m_n / emw.Torder_m_n and totals as RTtotal. Additional subnodes (Wave Equation, Electric, PEC, PMC, IBC, TBC, layered conditions) can be added under the Periodic Structure.

tools.name: Reference Direction (Periodic Structure, Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Default subnode of Periodic Structure that fixes the first in-plane reference direction a1 of the unit cell, from which the second direction a2, the primitive vectors b1/b2 and the azimuth angle of incidence are derived. In 3D select an edge (a1 is parallel to it) and an origin point from which a1 points away; in 2D select a point on the excited port boundary.
tools.usage: Periodic Structure 1 > Reference Direction 1 (default subnode); Edge Selection and Origin (3D) or Point Selection (2D). Type string: ReferenceDirection (tag rdir1).

parameters.name: Edge Selection (3D)
parameters.description: Edge of the excited port along which a1 is aligned.

parameters.name: Origin (3D) / Point Selection (2D)
parameters.description: Point from which a1 points away.

tools.example: For a hexagonal metasurface cell: select one hexagon edge of the top port in Reference Direction 1 and the vertex at its start as Origin; the azimuth angle alpha2 is then measured from that edge. Application Library: RF_Module/Tutorials/hexagonal_grating
tools.notes: Variables emw.aUnit1x..z and emw.aUnit2x..z expose the reference directions; emw.b1x/emw.G1x the primitive and reciprocal lattice vectors.

tools.name: Floquet Periodic Condition (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Periodic boundary pair with the Bloch-Floquet phase shift E_dst = E_src*exp(-i*kF.(r_dst - r_src)), where kF is the tangential wave vector of the incident plane wave. It is created automatically for every pair of opposite side walls of a Periodic Structure and normally takes kF from the periodic port; the general Periodic Condition node offers the same Floquet option plus Continuity, Antiperiodicity and Cyclic symmetry (sector angle and azimuthal mode number).
tools.usage: Periodic Structure > Floquet Periodic Condition (default subnodes), or Physics > Boundaries > Periodic Condition > Type of periodicity: Floquet periodicity. API: physics("emw").create("pc1", "PeriodicCondition", 2); feature("pc1").set("PeriodicType", "Floquet"); set("Floquet_source", "UserDefined"); set("kFloquet", new String[]{"k_x", "k_y", "0"})

parameters.name: Floquet_source
parameters.description: FromPeriodicPort (default in Periodic Structure) or UserDefined.

parameters.name: k-vector for Floquet periodicity kFloquet
parameters.description: Tangential wave vector (rad/m) for UserDefined, e.g. swept for band diagrams.

parameters.name: PeriodicType (general node)
parameters.description: Continuity, Antiperiodicity, Floquet, or Cyclic symmetry (sector angle automatic/user, azimuthal mode number m).

tools.notes: Use identical meshes on source and destination (the physics-controlled mesh does this; otherwise Mesh > Copy Face). A Periodic Condition with Floquet type is already catalogued generically as 'Periodic Condition (electromagnetics)'.

tools.name: Specific Absorption Rate (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: 3D domain feature that computes the specific absorption rate SAR = Q/rho (W/kg) from the electromagnetic loss density and the tissue mass density, the dosimetric quantity required for RF exposure compliance of phones, Wi-Fi devices and MRI coils. Besides the local variable emw.SAR, averaged variables such as emw.SAR1g are available for regulatory 1-gram averaging.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Specific Absorption Rate. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("sar1", "SpecificAbsorptionRate", 3); feature("sar1").set("rho_mat", "userdef"); set("rho", "1000[kg/m^3]")

parameters.name: Density rho (rho, rho_mat)
parameters.description: From material (default) or User defined.

tools.notes: Normalize the source (port input power Pin) to the transmitter's real output power before reporting SAR. Couple with Heat Transfer (Microwave Heating / Bioheat) to obtain the temperature rise.

tools.name: Perfect Electric Conductor and Impedance Boundary Condition on Domains (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Domain-level versions of the PEC and Impedance Boundary Condition (types DomainPerfectElectricConductor and DomainImpedance): the physics is switched off inside the selected domains and the condition is applied automatically to their exterior boundaries. Selecting whole metal parts by domain is faster and less error prone than picking dozens of faces, especially for imported CAD with many small surfaces; the IBC version takes conductivity, permittivity and permeability of the excluded metal from its material.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Domains > Perfect Electric Conductor / Impedance Boundary Condition. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("pec2", "DomainPerfectElectricConductor", 3); physics("emw").create("imp2", "DomainImpedance", 3)

parameters.name: Surface impedance definition (DomainImpedance)
parameters.description: From material properties (sigma, epsr, mur of the excluded domain) or User defined surface impedance.

parameters.name: Skin Depth Calculator
parameters.description: Conductivity or resistivity, epsr, mur and frequency -> computed skin depth (for example 0.65 um for 6e7 S/m at 10 GHz).

tools.notes: The IBC is valid only when the skin depth is small compared with the conductor size and curvature; otherwise mesh the conductor with Wave Equation, Electric. The toolbar button 'Lossy Feature from Materials' adds TBC/IBC nodes automatically from the materials.

tools.name: Electric Field (Electromagnetic Waves boundary condition)
tools.description: Boundary (also edge/point) constraint n x E = n x E0 that prescribes the tangential electric field; the normal component is left free. It is mainly for special situations such as imposing a known field on a cut or a field computed elsewhere, and should generally not be used to excite a model because it reflects all waves - Port, Lumped Port or Scattering Boundary Condition are the absorbing alternatives. PEC is its special case E0 = 0.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Electric Field. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("efb1", "ElectricField", 2)

parameters.name: Electric field E0
parameters.description: Vector components in V/m.

parameters.name: Constraint Settings (advanced)
parameters.description: Standard/weak constraint options.

tools.notes: Available in emw, Beam Envelopes (for each wave envelope E01/E02), Boundary Elements and Time Explicit interfaces.

tools.name: Magnetic Field (Electromagnetic Waves boundary condition)
tools.description: Exterior-boundary condition n x H = n x H0 that prescribes the tangential magnetic field, the natural (Neumann-type) counterpart of the Electric Field condition; H0 = 0 is equivalent to a Perfect Magnetic Conductor. Use it to impose a known surface magnetic field, for example from an analytic solution or a coupled model.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Magnetic Field. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("mfb1", "MagneticFieldBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Magnetic field H0
parameters.description: Vector components in A/m.

tools.notes: In the Time Explicit interface the same node exists under the type MagneticField; in Beam Envelopes H01/H02 are given per wave.

tools.name: Matched Boundary Condition (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Low-reflecting exterior boundary that is transparent to a wave with a known scattered (outgoing) direction ks,dir, so unlike the Scattering Boundary Condition it absorbs well even at large angles to the boundary normal; it is also transparent to an incoming wave. It can launch an incident field given by E, H or a Gaussian beam (paraxial, with waist radius and focal distance), with a Reference Point subnode setting the phase reference.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Matched Boundary Condition. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewfd").create("mbc1", "MatchedBoundaryCondition", 1); feature("mbc1").set("IncidentField", "GaussianBeam")

parameters.name: IncidentField
parameters.description: NoIncidentField (default), EField, HField or GaussianBeam.

parameters.name: Incident wave direction kdir / Scattered wave direction kScaDir
parameters.description: Defaults: inward normal and outward normal.

parameters.name: Gaussian beam w0, p0, inputQuantity (Eg0 or inputPower)
parameters.description: Beam waist radius (default 20*pi/k0, i.e. 10 wavelengths), distance to focal plane, field amplitude or power.

parameters.name: NoScatteredField
parameters.description: Suppresses spurious scattered solutions between unconstrained boundaries.

tools.notes: In 2D axisymmetry the incident direction must be parallel to the axis and a Symmetry Axis Reference Point subnode is added. The Beam Envelopes interface has its own Matched Boundary Condition that takes the direction from the prescribed phase.

tools.name: Reference Point and Symmetry Axis Reference Point (Electromagnetic Waves incident-field subnodes)
tools.description: Point subnodes of the Scattering and Matched boundary conditions (and Beam Envelopes boundaries) that define the reference position r_ref used in the incident-field phase, E0*exp(-j*k*kdir.(r - r_ref)), and the axis origin of an incident Gaussian beam. Without them the average position of the boundary selection is used; in 2D axisymmetry a Symmetry Axis Reference Point at the intersection with the axis is added by default.
tools.usage: Right-click Scattering Boundary Condition / Matched Boundary Condition > Reference Point. API: physics("ewfd").feature("sctr1").create("rpnt1", "ReferencePoint", 0)

parameters.name: Point Selection
parameters.description: Reference position is the average of the selected points.

parameters.name: Definition
parameters.description: Point selection (default) or User defined r0 (must lie on the parent boundary).

tools.notes: Only available when the parent defines an incident field. Types: ReferencePoint (rpnt) and SymmetryAxisReferencePoint (srpnt).

tools.name: Surface Magnetic Current Density (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Boundary source that prescribes a surface magnetic current density Jms0 (V/m) on exterior or interior boundaries, producing a jump in the tangential electric field. It is the dual of the Surface Current Density and is useful for equivalent-aperture (magnetic frill) excitations and Huygens-surface sources; only the tangential part of the vector is used.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Surface Magnetic Current Density. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("smcd1", "SurfaceMagneticCurrentDensity", 2)

parameters.name: Surface magnetic current density Jms0
parameters.description: Vector in V/m, projected onto the boundary.

parameters.name: Surface Current Density subnode
parameters.description: One-sided electric surface current on interior boundaries (side up/down).

tools.notes: Constraint Settings are available under Advanced Physics Options.

tools.name: Surface Roughness (Electromagnetic Waves impedance and transition subnode)
tools.description: Subnode of the Impedance and Transition boundary conditions that increases the effective surface impedance of a conductor to account for copper roughness, which raises conductor loss at microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies. The Sawtooth model (Hammerstad-Jensen) uses the RMS roughness; the Snowball model (Huray) uses a hexagonal cell area and a table of snowball radii and counts.
tools.usage: Right-click Impedance Boundary Condition or Transition Boundary Condition > Surface Roughness. API: physics("emw").feature("imp1").create("srf1", "SurfaceRoughness", 2)

parameters.name: Surface roughness model
parameters.description: Sawtooth (default, Delta_RMS in m) or Snowball (A_hex plus table of radius and number of snowballs).

parameters.name: Skin depth type
parameters.description: Physics-controlled (default) or User defined delta.

parameters.name: Side
parameters.description: Upside or Downside for the Transition Boundary Condition.

tools.example: PCB microstrip at 28 GHz: Transition Boundary Condition on the copper trace (d = 35[um]) > Surface Roughness > Sawtooth, Delta_RMS = 1.2[um]; compare emw.S21dB with and without the subnode.
tools.notes: Both models only scale the smooth-surface impedance; they do not resolve the geometry of the roughness.

tools.name: Layered Transition Boundary Condition (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Interior-boundary condition that represents a stack of geometrically thin layers defined by a Layered Material (Layered Material Link, Layered Material Stack or a Single Layer Material): for each layer the transfer and surface impedances are computed from its thickness and material, relating the jump in tangential E to the surface currents on both sides. Use it for multilayer metallization, coated sheets, thin films and resistive-plus-dielectric sandwiches that would be too thin to mesh.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Layered Transition Boundary Condition (after defining a Layered Material on the boundaries). API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("ltbc1", "LayeredTransitionBoundaryCondition", 2)

parameters.name: Shell Properties (Use all layers)
parameters.description: Couple to all layered materials or pick one; Layer Cross Section Preview / Layer 3D Preview buttons.

parameters.name: Electric displacement field model
parameters.description: Relative permittivity, Refractive index, loss tangent models, Dielectric loss, Drude-Lorentz or Debye - isotropic only; values From material per layer or one User defined value for all layers.

tools.example:
Rat-race coupler with gold-on-copper traces: define a Layered Material Stack (Cu 17 um + Au 1 um) on the trace boundaries, then add Layered Transition Boundary Condition 1 with 'Use all layers'.
Application Library: RF_Module/Couplers_and_Power_Dividers/rat_race_coupler
tools.notes: Assumes near-normal propagation in the layers and thickness smaller than the radius of curvature; not compatible with Mode Analysis. Absorbed power: emw.ltbc1.Ploss.

tools.name: Layered Impedance Boundary Condition (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Exterior-boundary condition for a stack of thin layers on top of a thick substrate that is itself not meshed: the layers are handled like a Layered Transition Boundary Condition and the substrate by an Impedance Boundary Condition. It models coated mirrors, dielectric-on-metal reflectors and absorber coatings on large metal bodies without meshing either the films or the metal.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Layered Impedance Boundary Condition. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewfd").create("libc1", "LayeredImpedanceBoundaryCondition", 1); feature("libc1").set("substrateMaterial", "mat2")

parameters.name: Shell Properties (allLayers)
parameters.description: Layered Material the condition is coupled to.

parameters.name: Layer Properties
parameters.description: Displacement field model of the thin layers (From material per layer).

parameters.name: Substrate Properties (substrateMaterial, surfaceImpedanceDefinition)
parameters.description: Substrate material and its displacement field model, or a User defined surface impedance (default Z0_const).

tools.notes: Material properties must be isotropic; absorbed power is available as emw.libc1.Ploss (or ewfd.libc1.Ploss) and absorptance emw.libc1.A.

tools.name: Cable Shield (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Interior-boundary condition that models the braided or tubular shield of a cable as a thin layer defined by a transfer impedance, relating the jump in tangential E across the shield to the induced surface current. It is used for shielding-effectiveness and cable-coupling (EMI/EMC) studies where the shield is geometrically thin but not electrically thin; lumped ports and elements may terminate on it.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Cable Shield (interior boundaries). API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("cshield1", "CableShield", 2)

parameters.name: Cable shield type
parameters.description: Tube (default, thickness d = 0.2 mm), Perforated tube (thickness, holes per meter = 10, hole radius Rh = 0.5 mm, Rh > d) or User defined transfer impedance per meter (default 0.01 ohm/m).

parameters.name: Cable shield radius Rcable
parameters.description: Default 2 mm.

parameters.name: Electric conductivity
parameters.description: From material by default.

parameters.name: Resonance Constraint / Skin Depth Calculator
parameters.description: Same options as the Transition Boundary Condition.

tools.example: Coax cable crossing a slotted enclosure: apply Cable Shield (Perforated tube, v = 40 holes/m, Rh = 0.4[mm]) to the outer-conductor surface and evaluate emw.cshield1.Ploss and the induced port voltage.
tools.notes: Power absorbed in the shield: emw.cshield1.Ploss; absorptance emw.cshield1.A. Frequency Domain interface only.

tools.name: Symmetry Plane (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Exterior-boundary condition representing a field symmetry cut of type Zero tangential electric field (PEC) or Zero tangential magnetic field (PMC). Compared with plain PEC/PMC nodes it tells far-field calculations, lumped ports (characteristic impedance adjustment) and Touchstone export about the reduction, so results are reported for the full structure; the interface toolbar can create half-symmetry models automatically.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Symmetry Plane, or interface toolbar Convert to a Half-Symmetry Model (PEC/PMC XY-, YZ-, ZX-symmetry Plane). API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("symp1", "SymmetryPlane", 2); feature("symp1").set("Symmetry_type", "pmc"); physics("emw").prop("Toolbar").runCommand("PECXYSymmetryPlane")

parameters.name: Symmetry_type
parameters.description: pec (only normal E on the plane) or pmc (only tangential E on the plane).

tools.notes: Check the polarization of every excited and scattered mode: a PMC cut through a TE20 waveguide satisfies the transverse port field but wrongly suppresses the longitudinal H component. With Far-Field Domain, Inhomogeneous only one symmetry plane is allowed.

tools.name: Magnetic Current (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Line source of magnetic current Im (unit V) applied to edges in 3D or to points (out-of-plane current) in 2D and 2D axisymmetry; for a single line the electric field circulates around the line. It is the classic way to model a coaxial aperture as a magnetic frill in antenna feeds and to create TE-type line sources.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Edges (3D) or Points (2D/2D-axi) > Magnetic Current. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("mc1", "MagneticCurrent", 1)

parameters.name: Magnetic current Im
parameters.description: Amplitude in V.

tools.notes: For electric line currents use Edge Current (3D) or Line Current (Out-of-Plane) (2D). No S-parameters are computed; normalize with the radiated power instead.

tools.name: Edge Current (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Electric line current I0 along edges in 3D, used to model thin wires, lightning channels and discharge paths without meshing their cross section. In the Electromagnetic Waves, Transient interface the current can be a built-in pulse: Electrostatic discharge (human body, extended human body, machine or charged device model) or Lightning (double-exponential with amplitude and rise/decay constants), propagating along a parameterized path with a given velocity.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Edges > Edge Current. API: model.component("comp1").physics("temw").create("edc1", "EdgeCurrent", 1); feature("edc1").set("CurrentPulseType", "Lightning")

parameters.name: Edge current I0 (Ie)
parameters.description: Frequency domain amplitude in A, or User defined time function in temw.

parameters.name: CurrentPulseType (temw)
parameters.description: UserDefined, ElectrostaticDischarge or Lightning; Plot Pulse Shape button.

parameters.name: ElectrostaticDischargePulseModel
parameters.description: HumanBodyModel (default), ExtendedHumanBodyModel, machine or charged-device model with their amplitudes and time constants.

parameters.name: Lightning parameters
parameters.description: LightningPulseAmplitude (30 kA), rise time constant (0.454 us), decay time constant (143 us), parameters 1 and 2.

parameters.name: Parameterized path / Pulse velocity v_p / reverseDirection
parameters.description: Automatic path s1 or User defined; default velocity c_const.

tools.notes: Available in emw and temw (and point versions in 2D via Line Current (Out-of-Plane)). The mesh along the edge must resolve the shortest wavelength in the pulse spectrum.

tools.name: Electric Point Dipole (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Point source representing an infinitesimal current filament with dipole moment p = I*d (A*m), specified as magnitude and direction or as a vector. It is the standard source for Hertzian-dipole validation, quantum-emitter and nanoantenna studies (Purcell factor, near-field enhancement) and for exciting cavities without a physical feed.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Points > Electric Point Dipole. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewfd").create("epd1", "ElectricPointDipole", 0); feature("epd1").set("DipoleSpecification", "MagnitudeAndDirection")

parameters.name: DipoleSpecification
parameters.description: MagnitudeAndDirection (direction np, magnitude p) or DipoleMoment (vector p).

parameters.name: Electric current dipole moment p
parameters.description: A*m; in 2D axisymmetry only the z component on the axis.

tools.notes: In 2D it requires Three-component or In-plane field components and zero out-of-plane wave number; in 2D axisymmetry azimuthal mode number 0. The background-field formulation also offers an electric point dipole wave type (ebem).

tools.name: Magnetic Point Dipole (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Point source representing a small circular current loop in the limit of vanishing area at fixed product I*a, with magnetic dipole moment m (m^2*A). Use it for loop-antenna and RFID-tag near-field studies, magnetic resonance of particles and as a dual source to the electric dipole.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Points > Magnetic Point Dipole (3D and 2D). API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("mpd1", "MagneticPointDipole", 0)

parameters.name: Dipole specification
parameters.description: Magnitude and direction (nm, m) or Dipole moment (vector m).

tools.notes: In 2D only with Three-component or Out-of-plane field components and zero out-of-plane wave number.

tools.name: Line Current (Out-of-Plane) (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Point source in 2D and 2D axisymmetric models that represents a current I0 flowing perpendicular to the modeling plane (z-direction in 2D, azimuthal direction in 2D axisymmetry). It produces TE-type cylindrical waves and is the quickest way to excite 2D scattering and waveguide problems or to model a loop in axisymmetry.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Points > Line Current (Out-of-Plane). API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("lco1", "LineCurrentOutOfPlane", 0)

parameters.name: Out-of-plane current I0
parameters.description: Amplitude in A.

tools.notes: Also available in Electromagnetic Waves, Transient (2D and 2D-axi).

tools.name: Continuity (Electromagnetic Waves pair condition)
tools.description: Pair condition that enforces continuity of the tangential field across identity pairs created when the geometry ends in Form Assembly instead of Form Union, so non-conforming meshes on both sides behave as one domain. A default Continuity node is added to the electromagnetic-wave interfaces and to the Transmission Line interface.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Pairs > Continuity (requires an Identity Pair); a default instance (tag dcont1) is created automatically when the geometry is an assembly. Type string: Continuity; pair selection properties pairSelection (all) and pairs.

parameters.name: Pair Selection
parameters.description: All pairs or a list of identity pairs.

parameters.name: Constraint Settings
parameters.description: Pointwise/symmetric constraint options (advanced).

tools.example:
Rotating-joint or moving-part model built as an assembly: Geometry > Form Union/Assembly > Action = Form an assembly; the default Continuity (dcont1) pair condition links the two sides.
Application Library: RF_Module/Antenna_Arrays/microstrip_patch_antenna_inset (default dcont1 node)
tools.notes: Accuracy is best when the meshes on both sides of the pair are similar. The Geometrical Optics equivalent is Ray Continuity.

tools.name: Gaussian Beam Background and Input Fields (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Built-in Gaussian beam available as background field (scattered-field formulation) and as incident field in Scattering, Matched and Beam Envelopes boundary conditions. The Paraxial approximation is valid for waists much larger than the wavelength; Plane wave expansion sums many plane waves (default Nk = 13 per transverse dimension, so 2*13*13 = 338 plane waves in 3D) and is exact for tightly focused beams, optionally including evanescent components. The same Formulation section also offers linearly polarized plane waves defined by roll, pitch and yaw angles, and in 2D axisymmetry linearly polarized plane waves expanded in azimuthal modes.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain > Formulation = Scattered field > Background wave type = Gaussian beam. API: physics("ewfd").prop("BackgroundField").set("SolveFor", "scatteredField"); prop("BackgroundField").set("WaveType", "GaussianBeam"); prop("BackgroundField").set("GaussianBeamType", "PlaneWaves"); prop("BackgroundField").set("w0", "w0")

parameters.name: GaussianBeamType
parameters.description: Paraxial (default) or PlaneWaves (plane wave expansion).

parameters.name: BeamOrientation, w0, p0
parameters.description: Xaxis/Yaxis/Zaxis; beam waist radius (default 20*pi/k0 = 10 wavelengths); focal plane position.

parameters.name: Ebg / inputQuantity / inputPower
parameters.description: Transverse field amplitude at focus, or power with a non-normalized amplitude.

parameters.name: WaveVectorDistributionType, WaveVectorCount, ktMax, allowEvanescentWaves
parameters.description: Automatic or userdef expansion; count Nk (odd, default 13); maximum transverse wave number (default 2*sqrt(2*log(10))/w0).

parameters.name: kUserDefined
parameters.description: Wave number k (sign sets the propagation direction; default k0).

parameters.name: Linear pol. plane wave: Eampl, angleRoll, anglePitch, angleYaw
parameters.description: 3D plane wave from successive roll/pitch/yaw rotations; 2D-axi: incAngle, polAngle, highestMode with the Set up Sweep button (modeNum).

tools.notes: A paraxial beam is not an exact Helmholtz solution, so a tightly focused paraxial background gives a nonzero scattered field even without a scatterer. Too few plane waves (small Nk relative to ktMax) create periodic replicas of the beam. The background field must solve the wave equation in the domains adjacent to the absorbing boundaries.

tools.name: RF Module Part Library (connectors, coplanar waveguides, SMD pads, waveguides)
tools.description: Collection of parameterized geometry parts for RF models that can be inserted as Part Instances: SMA and edge-launch connectors (for example connector_sma_flange2, connector_sma_pcb_mount, edge-launch ELF/TLF/VLF series with full and simplified versions), coplanar-waveguide straights, 90/180-degree bends and transitions for PCB and on-chip processes, surface-mount pads (0201, 0402, 0603 inch sizes) and waveguide parts. The parts carry selections for the conductive boundaries, so PEC and port conditions can be assigned in one click.
tools.usage: Windows > Part Libraries > RF Module > Connectors / Coplanar_Waveguides / Surface_Mount_Devices / Waveguides > select part > Add to Geometry; edit the input parameters in the Part Instance node. Files are under <COMSOL>/parts/RF_Module/.

parameters.name: Part input parameters
parameters.description: For example outer/inner radii of the coaxial structure, trace width and gap of a CPW, pad dimensions.

parameters.name: Selections to keep
parameters.description: Exported selections for conductors, dielectric and port faces become available in the component.

tools.example:
SMA-connectorized Wilkinson power divider:
1. Part Libraries > RF Module > Connectors > SMA_Connectors > connector_sma_flange2 > Add to Geometry (three instances, rotated/moved).
2. Use the part's conductor selection in a Domain PEC and its port face in a Coaxial Port.
Application Libraries: RF_Module/Couplers_and_Power_Dividers/wilkinson_power_divider, branch_line_coupler, RF_Module/Filters/cpw_resonator
tools.notes: Parts are built from partially parameterized geometry sequences; generic part-instance mechanics are described under the core Part Libraries entry.

tools.name: RF Module Material Library (PCB laminates and RF substrates)
tools.description: Material library with frequency-domain dielectric data (relative permittivity and loss tangent) for commercial RF, microwave and millimeter-wave substrates, supplied by the manufacturers. It includes Rogers (RO4000, RO3000, RT/duroid, TMM, TC, Kappa 438, CuClad/IsoClad, DiClad, CLTE, AD series, Radix, Anteo, MAGTREX 555), Isola (for example Astra MT77, I-Tera MT40, FR408HR, Tachyon 100G), Avient PREPERM, Garlock WavePro, Corning alumina ribbon ceramic, HYMAG'IN FILAMAG-F, Inkbit COT and Zetamix filaments.
tools.usage: Home > Add Material > RF > (manufacturer) > (product) > Add to Component, then select the substrate domains; Wave Equation, Electric picks up the data with 'From material' (use a loss-tangent displacement model).

parameters.name: Relative permittivity (real part) and loss tangent
parameters.description: Stored as material properties used by the Loss tangent displacement field models.

tools.example: Patch antenna on Rogers RO4003C: Add Material > RF > Rogers Corporation > RO4003C > assign to the substrate; set Wave Equation, Electric 2 > Electric displacement field model = Loss tangent, dissipation factor (From material).
tools.notes: Data are nominal datasheet values at the vendor's reference frequency; for broadband causal behavior consider a Wideband Debye fit.

tools.name: Wave Optics Module Part Library (slab and rectangular dielectric waveguides)
tools.description: Fully parameterized dielectric waveguide parts for photonic integrated circuits: 2D slab waveguides (straight, bend, S-bend, taper, straight-to-ring coupler, S-bend directional coupler) and 3D rectangular waveguides (straight, bend, S-bend, taper, straight-to-ring coupler, cross section). Parts define selections for core and cladding domains and for port boundaries, and the 3D parts define work planes so segments can be chained end to end.
tools.usage: Windows > Part Libraries > Wave Optics Module > Slab_Waveguides or Rectangular_Waveguides > part > Add to Geometry. Files are under <COMSOL>/parts/Wave_Optics_Module/.

parameters.name: Core and cladding widths, element length, core offset
parameters.description: Typical inputs of slab_waveguide_straight and its siblings.

parameters.name: Selections
parameters.description: Core, cladding, input/output port boundaries and mesh helper selections.

tools.example:
Ring resonator notch filter:
1. Add slab_waveguide_straight_to_ring_coupler and slab_waveguide_bend parts.
2. Assign core/cladding materials via the part selections and use Numeric Ports on the port selections with Boundary Mode Analysis.
Application Libraries: Wave_Optics_Module/Couplers_Filters_and_Mirrors/optical_ring_resonator(_3d), Wave_Optics_Module/Waveguides/tapered_waveguide, Wave_Optics_Module/Modulators_and_Switches/mach_zehnder_modulator
tools.notes: Well suited to the Beam Envelopes interface, whose swept physics-controlled mesh follows the part's longitudinal direction.

tools.name: Ray Optics Module Part Library (lenses, mirrors, prisms and apertures)
tools.description: Parameterized optical component geometries for ray tracing: spherical lenses (plano-convex, plano-concave, equi-convex, equi-concave, meniscus, general and polygonal), aspheric lenses (even, odd and Q-type Qbfs/Qcon), cylindrical lenses, cemented doublets and triplets, mirrors (spherical, conic on/off-axis, paraboloidal, aspheric, polygonal, elliptical planar, compound parabolic concentrators), a right-angle prism, a beam-splitter cube, a corner-cube retroreflector and circular/rectangular apertures and obstructions, plus 2D cylindrical lenses. Parts expose selections for the refracting/reflecting surfaces and clear apertures.
tools.usage: Windows > Part Libraries > Ray Optics Module > 3D (or 2D) > Spherical_Lenses / Aspheric_Lenses / Mirrors / Prisms / ... > part > Add to Geometry. Files are under <COMSOL>/parts/Ray_Optics_Module/.

parameters.name: Lens prescription inputs
parameters.description: Radii of curvature, center thickness, clear and physical diameters, conic constant and aspheric coefficients.

parameters.name: Position and orientation
parameters.description: Work-plane / displacement and rotation inputs used to build multi-element systems.

tools.example:
Double Gauss camera lens: insert spherical_lens_3d parts with the prescription from a parameter table, assign glasses from the Optical Material Library, release rays with Release from Grid (hexapolar) and plot a Spot Diagram.
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Lenses_Cameras_and_Telescopes/double_gauss_lens_geom_sequence, petzval_lens_geom_sequence, schmidt_cassegrain_telescope_geom_sequence
tools.notes: Legacy versions of several lenses are kept in the Legacy folder for old models. Use geometry shape order cubic (or higher) and 'Use geometry normals' for accurate refraction at curved surfaces.

tools.name: Optical Material Library (glass catalogs and dispersion data for Wave and Ray Optics)
tools.description: Material library shipped with the Wave Optics and Ray Optics Modules containing optical glasses from Schott, Ohara, CDGM and Corning (with dispersion-model coefficients such as Sellmeier or Schott, internal transmittance at 5/10/25 mm and Schott thermo-optic coefficients), plus organic, inorganic and miscellaneous materials and metals derived from the refractiveindex.info database. Geometrical Optics can detect the dispersion model per domain automatically, and the wave interfaces read n and k From material.
tools.usage: Home > Add Material > Optical > (Glasses by manufacturer / Inorganic / Organic / Metals ...) > Add to Component; Medium Properties > Refractive index of domains = Get dispersion model from material (Ray Optics) or Wave Equation, Electric > Refractive index From material (Wave Optics).

parameters.name: Dispersion model coefficients
parameters.description: For example DispersionModelSellmeierStandard, DispersionModelSellmeierModified, DispersionModelCauchy material models with reference temperature and pressure.

parameters.name: Internal transmittance
parameters.description: InternalTransmittance5/10/25 material models, converted automatically to an extinction coefficient.

parameters.name: Thermo-optic model
parameters.description: ThermoOpticDispersionModelSchott coefficients for temperature-dependent index.

tools.example:
Petzval lens with N-BK7/SF6-type glasses: add the glasses from Optical > Schott, set Medium Properties > Get dispersion model from material, and release polychromatic rays (486.1, 587.6, 656.3 nm) to see chromatic aberration.
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Lenses_Cameras_and_Telescopes/double_gauss_lens, Wave_Optics_Module/Optical_Scattering/scattering_nanosphere (gold n,k data)
tools.notes: Manufacturer indices are usually relative to air; COMSOL converts them to absolute indices with the Edlen air model at the stored reference temperature and pressure.
